results.title: Put your ideas to work with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
results.content:
Long-running agents need the right context at each step, so we built the Muse Wonder series with active memory, which carries important context across conversations, retrieves the right details for the task at hand, and keeps goals, constraints and earlier decisions available as work progresses.

Active focus helps agents keep working when a task gets difficult. The Muse Wonder series is trained to try alternative approaches, work through blockers and follow through to completion. It is also trained to ask for clarification when needed and check in before important actions, so developers can steer the model to better understand their intent and accomplish what they truly want. [...] ## TL;DR

 Muse Wonder - launching on Muse Code and Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million tokens, Muse Wonder brings comparable performance to Muse Wonder Full.
 Muse Wonder Full - available exclusively through the Power Usage and Maximum Usage Muse Code subscription plans, Muse Wonder Full is our most advanced model yet, bringing SOTA coding performance, long-running agents, and advanced computer-use capabilities to tackle developers’ most critical workflows.
 Muse Code Maximum Usage plan - a new subscription plan in Muse Code that includes 80x the Everyday Usage limit and access to Muse Wonder Full (also available in the Power Usage plan).

## Capabilities at the frontier

We built the Muse Wonder series to tackle the complex coding and agentic work that developers face every day: [...] Muse Wonder Full, available exclusively by subscription in Muse Code, gives developers a frontier model for their most complex workflows. Developers can start building with Muse Wonder Full on both the Power Usage plan and new Maximum Usage plan, which brings an 80x limit over the Everyday Usage plan and the same five-hour and weekly resets.

Install Muse Code today to start building:

curl -fsSL  | bash

For more details on the models and their research foundations, check out the Muse Wonder post on the AI at Meta blog.

results.title: Meta Launches Muse Wonder Series to Rival Anthropic, OpenAI Models - Business Insider
results.content:
Meta built its new AI models to complete complex multi-step tasks, such as disputing an insurance claim. To handle that, the AIs have features such as memory and the ability to try alternative approaches.

The Muse Wonder series was internally codenamed Watermelon, according to a person familiar with the matter.

In July, Business Insider reported that Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang had told staff that Watermelon had caught up to OpenAI.

"Watermelon uses an order of magnitude more compute than Avocado," he said at the time, referring to Meta's codename for Muse Spark, a prior family of models.

In the lead-up to Muse Wonder's launch, Zuckerberg and other Meta employees teased the release with watermelon-themed posts: [...] Meta has launched a new series of AI models, Muse Wonder, that it says has caught up to labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

"Muse Wonder is a much larger and more advanced class of models that brings us to the frontier," CEO Mark Zuckerberg posted on X on Monday.

It’s the latest sign that Meta’s big bet on AI — which has raised questions from investors — is paying off after the launch of its personal AI assistant, Muse. Meta is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, prompting some investor doubts earlier this year.

The Wonder series comes in two versions: Muse Wonder, a smaller, fast model Meta expects people to use for daily work, and Wonder Full, a larger and more capable version, the company said in a statement.

results.title: Meta Muse Wonder Explained: Active Memory, Active Focus, and the Hype | MindStudio
results.content:
Active focus addresses a different failure mode: agents that do fine on the first few steps of a task but stall the moment something unexpected happens. Meta says Muse Wonder was trained specifically not to give up when it hits a blocker, instead trying alternative approaches to still complete the task. Combined, these two features are the foundation of Meta’s pitch that this isn’t a model built to win trivia-style benchmarks, but one built to carry out multi-step, long-running work on someone’s behalf.

## How does Muse Wonder perform on benchmarks? [...] Active memory lets the model retain and recall relevant context about a user over long periods (days to months). Active focus is training aimed at persistence, so the model tries alternative approaches when it hits a blocker instead of stopping.

### How does Muse Wonder compare to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT6 Astra?

On Artificial Analysis’s intelligence index, Muse Wonder Full scored 56 versus Opus 5.5’s 58, putting it just behind the top model and ahead of GPT6 Astra on several individual benchmarks, including Deep SWE 1.1 and the Vals professional-task index.

### Is Muse Wonder benchmaxed? [...] ## What is Meta Muse Wonder?

Muse Wonder is Meta’s first model that the company itself calls “frontier class,” released on October 12 by Meta Super Intelligence Labs alongside a larger sibling called Muse Wonder Full. Muse Wonder is available through Meta’s model API and inside Muse Code, Meta’s terminal based coding agent. Muse Wonder Full, the bigger and reportedly stronger of the two, is not available via API at all. It only ships through a Muse Code subscription on the $50 or $200 monthly plans. Both were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in Ohio, and Muse Wonder is slated to power the standalone Muse app, rolling out to subscribers first.
